review: intriguing story, great live action character actors, great graphics, lots of fun, creative puzzles, mind bending hidden object iamages.... the list goes on. Loved every one of the games in this series so far. It's a pity the one before this 'Dire Grove'in not available on Steam. And the version I downloaded from Big Fish would not work!!!

The production value is higher on this than a lot of HOGs-- the actors are quite fun, in this game-- but the puzzles are often introduced with no sense of what the goal of the puzzle is. I had to rely on hints more than I wanted to compensate. Additionally, a few of the puzzles were a little too much for my tastes-- several were either too long for me, or just really boring overall. Of course hidden object games can have a puzzle or two you don't enjoy, but this one seemed to have more than usual. I'm a very casual HOG player, though, so that may be more reflective of me than an issue with the game. Still, this is my least favorite hidden object game I've played, which is sad because it clearly was made with a lot of care. I just wish the extra challenge felt fun instead of under-explained or tedious.
I miss when games were genuinely made with love like this and not some corporate procedure like the newer installments.

Détective privé de votre état, vous intervenez dans une histoire de disparition lié à la légende d'un trésor de pirate dans un manoir délabré situé en Louisiane.

Si l'histoire est plutôt sympathique à suivre, le reste est lui...boff...
Pour ma part, j'ai eu du mal à le terminer car le gameplay est déplaisant sur le long terme et j'ai même utilisé la soluce afin d'en finir avec ce jeu dans certains moments de celui ci (Chercher les objets disséminés dans les scènes).

Pour commencer, graphiquement le jeu est sorti en 2007 ce qui signifie qu'il est de base en résolution 640x480... Imaginez sur un écran ultra large ce que cela donne ^^ Il reste toutefois visible mais le bord des caractères, par exemple, est un peu flou, il en est de même pour les objets.

Il y a quelques HOC mais surtout des puzzles dont beaucoup sont retords et qui demandent de la patience pour les résoudre mais là où j'ai fini par "craquer" c'est le fait de chercher des objets dans différentes scènes du jeu régulièrement. toutes les scènes restent disponibles et quand tu dois trouver 5 "trucs" cachés dans le décor et cela plusieurs fois, ça ma saoulé sérieusement. Le système de logique est calqué sur les point'n' click des années 90 (La cohérence n'est pas de mise ici) et on a une barre d'inventaire qui ressemblait plus à un moment un étalage d'épicerie qu'à celle d'un hidden moderne.  

La chose cool du jeu est son intégration de personnage réel dans les décors. Comme d'habitude, tous ne sont pas très doué pour le jeu d'acteur et cela donne un côté "nanar" que j'apprécie beaucoup.

Le doublage est en VO (anglais) et avec des sous-titres en anglais. Il y a un collectible à récupérer (des cartes) je crois mais je dois avouer que j'avais surtout envie de finir le jeu et que je n'ai pas vraiment fait attention à sa présence.

Les décors sont en général plutôt agréables mais passer son temps à les refaire pour essayer de trouver un objet devient énervant sur la longueur.

A sa sortie, le jeu devait être un bon jeu mais vu de 2026, c'est une galère à faire sans compter que visuellement il a vieillit. A faire mais pas en priorité, je dirait même en dernier ressort...

I've been playing MCF games for a long time, starting with Madame Fate, around the time that game came out. I've since gone back and played the first few games in the series, and also a fair few of the later ones.

To me, 13th Skull is the absolute pinnacle of the series, my most loved game of them all, and possibly the best Hidden Object Adventure I ever played.

The puzzles are good, starting with the "local" puzzles, and then also including the "meta" puzzles that span the majority of the game. The HO sections are OK, but have taken a backseat to the other gameplay elements. The atmosphere and music are through the roof! I am partial to pirates ("Everything. Is better. With Pirates!), but it's not just that, it's the whole southern vibe. the music. 

And then, the actors. The actors are amazing, and the performances are generally great and well directed. It just adds so much to the whole thing, even though I realise it might not be everyone's cup of tea.

My only gripe with this game is the bonus chapter, which feels kind of forced, and the final puzzle in it which is kind of non-intuitive, albeit pretty thematic.

I'm not sure what the purpose of this review is really. If you're into MCF games, you've either already played this, or have a strong opinion on it. If you're not into MCF games, then liking this game depends on your tastes. I had a lot of fun with it.

As a bonus, I recorded a playthrough of the game, with a friend, so anyone interested can take a peek here:

This is a tough one.  I'm going to say yes to recommend but gonna talk about a few things.

First, the game hasn't aged well tech wise.  It's very finicky and picky with the cursor or item placement and at one point you need to continuously zoom in then click and drag the map because you've multiple things to find, the map liked to close, a lot.  And, because of it's original age, you cannot lock the item bar, something that always drives me crazy especially when I need to place multiple things on the same screen.  The cursor being a bit off made a few of the dragging items around puzzles kind of a pain.  Was not a fan of the portrait pieces that could be moved as whole lines.  That was very frustrating and we ended up skipping it.  Though I do appreciate that we CAN skip them if we need.

I will say the acting was alright.  Everyone seemed to be really focused and trying hard.  Nothing was 'phoned in'. I cannot say if the accents or portrayals were at all cliche in cases since I lack knowledge of the culture of where this takes place, at least in detail, nothing felt like they were playing it up for laughs.  I had been surprised to see so much on camera and not just voice acting as are the case with most HO games.

I enjoyed the story, even if some of the back and forth in the house to 'do this for me before I help you' was kind of annoying.  [spoiler] Though having the maid ask us to pick up the trash that was all over the house since we slit the bag open then left it felt appropriate.  As the protag in one of these games you're rarely punished for things.[/spoiler]

The end of the game was very frustrating.  Any puzzles I'd not done yet (since several are not immediately  assigned as things that need doing along with the last set of puzzles, including the map thing, were made a million times more frustrating by [spoiler] having the male character yell at me every minute or so.  I get it, we're on a 'timer' here and yes I could have turned off the voices but it just made that section such hell because it [/spoiler] made it so much harder to concentrate.

I'll say the very ending was a bit of a shocker.

Overall, the game is okay.  I like the story, the actors have heart and some of the puzzles were neat but parts felt rather drawn out and it while runs on Windows 10, doesn't run the best.

I consider this a top shelf Hidden Object Game.  Not only is the story good, there's actually some logic to finding stuff.  Most HOGs will have you pick up random stuff that you suddenly need later.  This one has you pick up random things that are widely useful and will be needed several times each: scissors, wrench, hedge clippers, etc.  I noticed early on that there were things that looked like they should be picked up, but they weren't clickable.  Only later would I get the quest to find all those things and trying to remember where I saw them was a different spin.

The puzzles were challenging and pretty novel.  Part of it is figuring out what you have to do.  That's more realistic, but it can be frustrating since there's rarely a reset option after I've mashed buttons until I figured it out.

It's fun and worth your time.
